rationale: The buyer signal is real — professional developers on HN explicitly saying 'I would pay' for honest tooling is credible — but buyer_clarity is weak: 'developers frustrated by JetBrains' is a vibe, not a specific business role with a budget line, and this skews toward individual consumer purchases (low ARPU, high churn). More critically, the product itself is a clean IDE plugin or LSP-based experience, which requires non-trivial engineering effort (deep language-server integration, editor compatibility), cannot be built with Claude prompts + a landing page, and cannot be delivered or maintained hands-off — every new version, every language-server update, and every support ticket demands real engineering. This falls squarely below the build_gates for buildability_with_ai and operational_autonomy and doesn't clear the 5.5 validate threshold.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator running a Claude factory. Building a usable IDE plugin or LSP layer for Scala/Kotlin requires sustained software engineering work (editor protocol, language semantics, packaging for JetBrains Marketplace or VS Code), ongoing maintenance per upstream LSP changes, and hands-on developer support. There is no prompt-and-Stripe path here. If you want to serve frustrated developers, a better angle would be a newsletter or curated resource (non-monetizable at scale) rather than a competing tooling product.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (score 3, floor 6) and operational_autonomy (score 4, floor 7). Idea requires real engineering, not a Claude-based micro-service. Total 4.6 also below min_total_to_validate (5.5).
